beats.label: S1 · Six months after
beats.text: History professor Tom Mason serves as second-in-command of the 2nd Mass, a militia-and-civilian remnant of the alien invasion that killed 90% of humanity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the world, the unit, and Tom's role — the frame for everything that follows.

beats.label: S1 · Ben is out there
beats.text: On a supply run, Hal glimpses his missing middle brother Ben in a harnessed work column, confirming the aliens have enslaved him rather than killed him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ben's harnessing is the personal engine driving Tom's arc all season.

beats.label: S1 · Pope joins, Skitter caged
beats.text: Tom's squad captures outlaw leader Pope, who becomes camp cook and weapons tinkerer, and takes a live Skitter for Anne and Dr. Harris to study.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Pope as a permanent wildcard and opens the biology thread that reshapes what the enemy is.

beats.label: S1 · Ben rescued, not returned
beats.text: Hal infiltrates the hospital wearing a harness and pulls Ben out, but the boy wakes changed — stronger, faster, and quietly pulled toward the Skitters.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The rescue that should end Tom's storyline instead opens a new one: Ben isn't fully theirs.

beats.label: S1 · Clayton's Faustian bargain
beats.text: The 7th Mass's Clayton turns out to be trading children to the aliens for his camp's safety; the 2nd Mass kills him but loses Mike shielding the kids' escape.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows the invasion is corroding humans as much as killing them, and thins the leadership around Weaver.

beats.label: S1 · A third species
beats.text: Scouting the Boston structure, Tom and Weaver spot tall humanoid Overlords directing the Skitters, and Anne's autopsy suggests Skitters were themselves once harnessed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Redefines the enemy: Skitters are middle-management, and harnessed kids may be the next generation of them.

beats.label: S1 · Tom boards the ship
beats.text: The strike on the alien structure succeeds, but a harnessed Karen delivers an Overlord's ultimatum and Tom walks aboard their shuttle to keep Ben safe.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the exact situation season 2 opens on — Tom gone, Ben still turning, Weaver holding the unit.

cliffhanger.text: The Boston structure is destroyed, but Tom has voluntarily boarded an Overlord's shuttle with Karen to spare Ben, leaving Weaver standing in the street watching him go.
questions: What do the Overlords want with Tom specifically?
Is Ben still becoming something other than human?
Can Weaver hold the 2nd Mass together without its second-in-command?

characters.name: Tom Mason
characters.line: History professor turned 2nd Mass second-in-command; walked onto an alien shuttle at season's end to protect his sons.

characters.name: Captain Weaver
characters.line: Hard-edged commander of the 2nd Mass, grieving a daughter he had to kill after her harnessing, now leading alone.

characters.name: Hal Mason
characters.line: Tom's eldest, a capable fighter who rescued Ben from the hospital and is watching him carefully for signs of change.

characters.name: Ben Mason
characters.line: Tom's middle son, freed from a harness but left faster, stronger, and quietly drawn back toward the Skitters.

characters.name: Matt Mason
characters.line: Tom's youngest, the civilian child whose safety anchors most of Tom's decisions.

characters.name: Anne Glass
characters.line: Camp doctor who worked out how to kill a Skitter and whose autopsy hinted Skitters were once something else.

characters.name: Pope
characters.line: Ex-outlaw turned cook and improvised-weapons maker; the man who figured out how to punch through Mech armour.

characters.name: Karen
characters.line: Hal's girlfriend, captured and harnessed by the aliens, now used by the Overlords as a mouthpiece to Tom.

characters.name: Rick
characters.line: Mike's son, unharnessed but still loyal to the Skitters, actively trying to pull Ben back to them.
